newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business confidence at two-year peak in June.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business confidence at two-year peak in June.

text.p: U.S. business confidence shot up in June to its highest level in more than two years, sparked by the prospect of steady economic growth with minimal inflation, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce said on Friday.
Its bimonthly index of Business Confidence -- which measures the outlook for growth, employtment and sales over six months -- jumped to 58.9 in June from 56.5 in April, the last time it was compiled.
It was the highest level for the index since February 1995, when it hit 59.0. More than 4,000 firms were surveyed for opinion on the business outlook for the rest of 1997.
"Small businesses are expressing rising confidence because of the low-inflation, high-performance economy of the past several months," said Robert Barr, an economist with the business lobby group.

But he noted the increase in confidence was rooted in business' belief that the economy will keep growing, whereas the other two components of the index -- expected sales and hiring plans -- were weaker in June than was the case in April.
"Apparently, the nation's small businesses are signaling some caution even as their outlook for the overall economy improves," Barr said.
The index for the overall economy soared to 55.3 in June from 47.3 in April. But for sales it eased down to 64.2 from 64.9 in April and for employment it declined to 57.2 in June from 57.4 in April.
